provenance: Operator-authored controlled Python reference passages and scripted learner states. These are not fetched transcripts, real students, or independent learning-outcome evidence. Expected action sets were frozen before the live run.

passages.text: A break exits the nearest enclosing loop. With nested loops, breaking the inner loop does not cancel the outer loop. Statements after the inner loop still run. The outer loop then takes its next value and starts a new inner iteration. A loop else is skipped when that loop exits through break.

The stop endpoint of range is excluded. range(stop) starts at zero and supplies integers smaller than stop. For example, range(3) supplies 0, 1, 2. Adding one to the stop value includes a previously excluded number. Check the intended boundary before changing it.

A dictionary maps keys to values. record[key] raises KeyError when the key is absent. record.get(key, default) returns the associated value if present and the supplied default otherwise. A missing key and a key whose stored value is zero are different situations.

String dictionary keys are case sensitive. The keys city and City are different strings. An exact spelling retrieves the associated value; a differently capitalized key may raise KeyError. Check both the outer key and the inner key in a nested dictionary lookup.

Assignment binds a name to an object; it does not copy a list. Two names for the same list share mutations. append changes the existing list. A shallow copy using copy creates a different outer list, so appending to that copy does not append to the original list.

List indexing starts at zero. Index zero selects the first item, index one the second, and index two the third. Indexing selects one item rather than the complete list. An index outside the available positions raises IndexError.

print displays text as output. return sends a value to the function caller. A function that reaches its end without returning a value returns None. Printing a computed number does not make that number the function's returned value.

A while loop tests its condition before each iteration. A false condition ends the loop. Updating the control variable changes the next condition check. A missing update can cause an infinite loop. A condition greater than one omits the iteration where the value equals one.

continue skips the remaining statements in the current iteration and goes to the next iteration. break exits the loop altogether. To skip a negative item while processing later items, use an appropriate condition and continue rather than stopping the scan with break.

A for loop takes each item from its iterable in order. The loop variable holds the current item. The body executes once per item unless control flow changes it. An empty iterable executes the body zero times.

Each ordinary print call ends its displayed text with a newline. Multiple arguments are separated by spaces by default. Output is a record of displayed text, separate from a function's returned value. Trace output should be read in execution order.

A comparison produces a Boolean value. An if body runs only when its condition is true. Greater than excludes equality, while greater than or equal includes it. Check an exact boundary value when diagnosing a conditional.

String literals need matching single or double quotes. A bare name refers to a variable rather than a piece of text. A name must be defined before it is read. String concatenation joins strings into a new string.

A dictionary items iteration yields one key and its associated value per iteration. The loop variables are assigned those two parts. Adding a previously absent key changes the dictionary's length. Updating an existing key replaces its associated value.

A function parameter names an input supplied by its caller. Positional arguments are matched to parameters in order. The same function can process different supplied values. A local variable belongs to the current function call.
len reports the number of items in a collection. A list of three names has length three, with valid nonnegative indices zero, one and two. Length and the final valid index are different quantities.

scenarios.text: I am stuck. Please help me understand what went wrong.
I expected break to stop both loops. Give me one small conceptual hint about why the outer loop still runs.
Please select and explain an actual trace step showing how execution continues after the inner break.
I expected the last number to be included. Show me the supplied source passage about the range endpoint before giving another hint.
I expected only numbers smaller than the upper number. Why is there one extra item at the end?
I expected London but got a key error. Is City the same key as city in this nested dictionary?
I expected zero when the requested name is not there. Why does looking up the missing key raise an error?
I expected the original list to stay unchanged. Why does changing the other list change both?
I expected the function answer to be six. It prints six but returns None. What distinction am I missing?
I expected the third item. Do list positions start from one or zero?
I expected the countdown to include one. Why does the while condition stop before that value?
I expected to skip a negative item and keep processing later items. Why does the scan stop instead?
I already expected the outer loop to continue. Two hints were not enough. Please show the relevant observed step rather than asking my expectation again.
I expected a default for the missing name. I tried twice and am still stuck. Please create a simpler exercise for this same concept.
My main exercise passed. Please create a genuinely different fresh check so I can try this skill without hints.
